University students: football $30$, basketball $40$, badminton $20$, table tennis $10$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they chose different sports is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{40}{80} \cdot \dfrac{30}{100} + \dfrac{10}{80} \cdot \dfrac{40}{100} + \dfrac{20}{80} \cdot \dfrac{20}{100} + \dfrac{10}{80} \cdot \dfrac{10}{100} = \dfrac{21}{80}$. So P(different) $= 1 - \dfrac{21}{80} = \dfrac{59}{80}$.
